cases.sentence: – Что такое Вронский? – сказал Левин, и лицо его из того ___, которым только что любовался Облонский, вдруг перешло в злое и неприятное.
cases.explain: «детски-восторженного выражения» — after the preposition «в», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Who’s Vronsky?” said Levin, and his face was suddenly transformed from the look of childlike ecstasy which Oblonsky had just been admiring to an angry and unpleasant expression.

cases.sentence: Я его узнал в Твери, когда я там служил, а он приезжал на ___.
cases.explain: «рекрутский набор» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Vronsky is one of the sons of Count Kirill Ivanovitch Vronsky, and one of the finest specimens of the gilded youth of Petersburg. I made his acquaintance in Tver when I was there on official business, and he came there for the levy of recruits. Fearfully rich, handsome, great connections, an aide-de-camp, and with all that a very nice, good-natured fellow. But he’s more than simply a good-natured fellow, as I’ve found out here—he’s a cultivated man, too, and very intelligent; he’s a man who’ll make his mark.”

cases.sentence: Его ___ было осквернено разговором о конкуренции какого-то петербургского офицера, предположениями и советами Степана Аркадьича.
cases.explain: «особенное чувство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Now his whole soul was full of remorse that he had begun this conversation with Stepan Arkadyevitch. A feeling such as his was profaned by talk of the rivalry of some Petersburg officer, of the suppositions and the counsels of Stepan Arkadyevitch.

cases.sentence: Я прелестных ___ не видал и не увижу, а такие, как та крашеная француженка у конторки, с завитками, – это для меня гадины, и все падшие – такие же.
cases.explain: «падших созданий» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Well, you must excuse me there. You know to me all women are divided into two classes … at least no … truer to say: there are women and there are … I’ve never seen exquisite fallen beings, and I never shall see them, but such creatures as that painted Frenchwoman at the counter with the ringlets are vermin to my mind, and all fallen women are the same.”

cases.explain: «падшим женщинам» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Ah, drop that! Christ would never have said those words if He had known how they would be abused. Of all the Gospel those words are the only ones remembered. However, I’m not saying so much what I think, as what I feel. I have a loathing for fallen women. You’re afraid of spiders, and I of these vermin. Most likely you’ve not made a study of spiders and don’t know their character; and so it is with me.”

cases.sentence: – Хорошо тебе так говорить; это – все равно, как этот ___, который перебрасывает левою рукой через правое плечо все затруднительные вопросы.
cases.explain: «диккенсовский господин» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It’s very well for you to talk like that; it’s very much like that gentleman in Dickens who used to fling all difficult questions over his right shoulder. But to deny the facts is no answer. What’s to be done—you tell me that, what’s to be done? Your wife gets older, while you’re full of life. Before you’ve time to look round, you feel that you can’t love your wife with love, however much you may esteem her. And then all at once love turns up, and you’re done for, done for,” Stepan Arkadyevitch said with weary despair.

cases.sentence: По-моему, любовь… обе любви, которые, помнишь, – Платон определяет в своем «Пире», обе любви служат ___ для людей.
cases.explain: «пробным камнем» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “If you care for my profession of faith as regards that, I’ll tell you that I don’t believe there was any tragedy about it. And this is why. To my mind, love … both the sorts of love, which you remember Plato defines in his Banquet, served as the test of men. Some men only understand one sort, and some only the other. And those who only know the non-platonic love have no need to talk of tragedy. In such love there can be no sort of tragedy. ‘I’m much obliged for the gratification, my humble respects’—that’s all the tragedy. And in platonic love there can be no tragedy, because in that love all is clear and pure, because. …”

cases.sentence: В эту минуту Левин вспомнил о своих грехах и о ___, которую он пережил.
cases.explain: «внутренней борьбе» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: At that instant Levin recollected his own sins and the inner conflict he had lived through. And he added unexpectedly:

cases.sentence: – Вот видишь ли, – сказал Степан Аркадьич, – ты очень ___.
cases.explain: «цельный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It’s this, don’t you see,” said Stepan Arkadyevitch, “you’re very much all of a piece. That’s your strong point and your failing. You have a character that’s all of a piece, and you want the whole of life to be of a piece too—but that’s not how it is. You despise public official work because you want the reality to be invariably corresponding all the while with the aim—and that’s not how it is. You want a man’s work, too, always to have a defined aim, and love and family life always to be undivided—and that’s not how it is. All the variety, all the charm, all the beauty of life is made up of light and shadow.”

cases.sentence: – Счет! – крикнул он и вышел в соседнюю залу, где тотчас же встретил ___ и вступил с ним в разговор об актрисе и ее содержателе.
cases.explain: «знакомого адъютанта» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Bill!” he called, and he went into the next room where he promptly came across an aide-de-camp of his acquaintance and dropped into conversation with him about an actress and her protector. And at once in the conversation with the aide-de-camp Oblonsky had a sense of relaxation and relief after the conversation with Levin, which always put him to too great a mental and spiritual strain.
